text:
Marathon Petroleum stock rose 1.34% today to close at $388.15, extending a sharp rally over the past week as oil prices spiked on Middle East tensions. Brent crude climbed near $96 a barrel Wednesday after Iran struck back at U.S. allies in retaliation for American attacks, with tanker incidents reported near the Hormuz Strait raising concerns about supply disruption. Refiners like Marathon benefit when crude prices rise faster than finished fuel prices fall, improving their margins—and the company is running refineries at 97.4% capacity, positioned to capture that spread.

The stock's momentum also reflects broader optimism in U.S. energy policy: the Trump administration announced a major oil deal with Venezuela and pledged investments to boost production there, signaling sustained demand for refining and petroleum products. With oil in storage at relatively modest levels (718.6 million barrels) and refiners operating near flat-out, the market appears confident in both near-term margins and longer-term refining demand.
